text: In 1857, the company gave its Indian soldiers a new rifle.
To load it, you had to bite open a paper cartridge.
A rumor spread like fire.
The cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat, offensive to Hindus and Muslims alike.
At Meerut, soldiers who refused them were jailed.
Their comrades rose up, freed them, and marched to Delhi where they declared the old Mughal
Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar ruler of India again.
The revolt spread across the north and one of its fiercest leaders was a young widow
where the company had tried to retire, Rani Lakshmi Bhai of Chhansi.
When her husband died, the company refused to accept her adopted son as heir and simply
took her kingdom.
She was handed a pension and told to step aside.
In 1857, she stepped back in.
She led her troops on horseback and died fighting in her late twenties.
She became the most famous face of the revolt.
The British crushed the rising with terrible brutality. Whole villages were burned. The
Hadar Shah Zafar was exiled to Burma. The Mughal dynasty, after 330 years, was over.
London decided the company could not be trusted with India anymore. In 1858 the British crown
took over directly. The Raj had begun.
Your Majesty, India is now ruled by the Crown.
Splendid. And the company?
Closed, Your Majesty.
Then I shall need a new title.
Empress of India, Ma'am?
Hmm. Now that's a title.
